chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about a man whose nose bleeds: is it upon him to wash its interior, meaning the inside of the nose? He said: “It is only upon him to wash what is outwardly visible of it.”

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam giving the ruling
key_terms.بَاطِنَهُ: its inner part, referring to the interior of the nose
key_terms.جَوْفَ الْأَنْفِ: the inside cavity of the nose
key_terms.مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهُ: that which is outwardly apparent or visible
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ: to wash for purposes of removing impurity

ai.seo_question: If someone has a nosebleed, must he wash the inside of the nose or only what is visible?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ritual purity when blood flows from the nose. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that only the outwardly visible part must be washed, not the inner cavity of the nose.
